project.name: Acme Order Service (OpenEdge ABL → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 migration)
project.description:
Reference scaffold for the Progress OpenEdge ABL → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 migration of the Acme-ERP order/stock procedures (reserve-stock.p, post-batch.p, apply-discount.p, post-invoice.p, build-order-lines.p), generated from a signed openedge spec (spec/v1, schemaId=openedge) via Astra. Every public surface carries a @SpecClaim citing the signed claim id and a @TargetMapping documenting the intended Spring/JPA construct.
IMPORTANT — this project is deliberately framework-free at COMPILE time. The maven-sidecar builds OFFLINE against a baked ~/.m2 cache that contains only junit/assertj/mockito + the pinned Maven plugins (NO Spring, NO JPA on hosts with no egress — a SOC2 constraint). So the ABL→Spring mapping is expressed as a documented CONTRACT (@TargetMapping + ports) rather than a live @Component/@Repository, and the pure business logic (stock arithmetic, the Unknown-value guard, batch atomicity) is REAL Java that the JUnit suite exercises for keeps. There is NO source-execution equivalence gate for ABL — the Progress AVM is proprietary and no free runtime exists — so the golden-dataset extraction score and THIS test suite (property + example) are the verification, and that limitation is documented, not stubbed.
To promote this scaffold into a live Spring Boot project, add spring-boot-starter-data-jpa (see each @TargetMapping) and swap the ports for @Repository/@Service beans; the domain classes move over unchanged.
